strengths: Clearly motivated problem: principled layer selection for fine-tuning-based model editing is an underexplored gap
The GradRatio metric has intuitive justification grounded in gradient geometry (edit responsiveness vs. capability preservation)
Honest reporting of negative/mixed results — the LLaMA-3-8B degradation is disclosed upfront rather than buried, which is commendable
Adaptive threshold mechanism is a reasonable engineering addition to guard against early-layer catastrophic edits
weaknesses: Contribution ceiling is low: by the authors' own admission the method provides 'automation without improvement,' which is a weak empirical payoff for a venue submission
Evaluation breadth is insufficient — only two model families; results on a third model (e.g., Mistral or Gemma) would clarify whether the Qwen success or LLaMA failure is the norm
The 5.26 pp capability degradation on LLaMA-3-8B in math reasoning is consequential but not explained mechanistically; the paper surfaces the failure without diagnosing it
The adaptive threshold is introduced somewhat ad hoc — the selection criterion for 'structurally critical' layers lacks theoretical grounding or ablation
No analysis of sensitivity to the retain set distribution, which is central to the ratio's validity
The method selects layers 'adjacent to' manual heuristics rather than coinciding with them — the practical benefit of automation vs. a single cheap sweep is not clearly quantified

ai_detection.reasoning: The introduction follows a rigid template: background paragraph, gap paragraph, method paragraph, results paragraph, then exactly three bullet-point contributions with parallel structure. Prose is uniformly clean and formulaic with no stylistic variation, hedging idioms, or authorial voice. The '3-bullet contributions' closer is a strong AI-generation fingerprint, and the overall length and density are characteristic of a prompted LLM summary rather than organic scientific writing.
